Timestamp UTC: 2026-10-23T21:05:10.020882+00:00
Plain-reading hypothesis, written before any round-2 probing.
The strict P0 /api middleware immediately writes HTTP 403 without explicitly reading the POST body. The test sends a body and sometimes sees a reset while reading that response. Hypothesis: early rejection/body/connection handling, rather than the released-port startup gap, is associated with the reset. Prior successful /runs, intake, and runs show calls make a startup bind race a weaker explanation for this late POST.
Prediction: changing ONLY the blocked /api/annotations POST body to empty bytes, retaining POST and the exact HTTPError=403 assertion and all other test code, reduces reset failures to zero in 30 isolated runs. This is a client-side perturbation, not a server fix or proof of mechanism. Persisting resets contradicts the narrow body-dependent prediction. It cannot establish the exact TCP mechanism or rule out timing effects.
The Phase-2 example port-handoff change is not used: holding the socket while Go binds requires socket inheritance support; no tracked change is authorized. A scratch-only body perturbation tests the alternative suggested by the existing rejection handler.
